claims.text: Depositing a thin, conformal CeO2 layer will enhance low-temperature oxidation activity relative to the unmodified catalyst.
Depositing a thin, conformal CeO2 layer will improve resistance to H2O and NO poisoning.
Depositing a thin, conformal CeO2 layer will extend catalyst lifetime durability.
Adding CeO2 will not increase the catalyst's platinum-group-metal content.
Controlled atomic layer deposition can produce a uniform CeO2 overlayer a few nanometers thick on the catalyst surface.
The CeO2 overlayer will form oxygen-vacancy-rich nanoclusters on the catalyst surface.
The oxygen-vacancy-rich CeO2 nanoclusters will act as an oxygen reservoir.
The CeO2 overlayer will act as a sintering-resistant barrier.
The CeO2 layer will enhance oxygen storage and redox cycling.
Enhanced oxygen storage and redox cycling will lower the activation barrier for CO and hydrocarbon oxidation at low temperatures.
The CeO2 layer will mitigate adsorption of H2O and NO poisoning species.
The CeO2 layer will help maintain structural integrity during thermal cycling and long-term aging.
The CeO2-modified catalyst will have a lower CO and hydrocarbon light-off temperature than the unmodified catalyst.
The CeO2-modified catalyst will have higher conversion efficiency in the presence of H2O and NO than the unmodified catalyst.
The CeO2-modified catalyst will undergo less sintering and activity loss after accelerated aging than the unmodified catalyst.
The anticipated benefits apply during transient operation below 150 °C in exhaust containing typical concentrations of H2O and NO and after accelerated lifetime-simulating aging.
